summary: A reflective first-person essay on birdwatching at four wildlife watching spots during autumn 2023, each paired with a local enthusiast or expert. The author meets Bob McAllister, Emily Waters, James Fielding and Andrea Zhang, who each find calm, patience, community or mindfulness through observing birds. The piece presents wildlife watching as a way to slow down and connect with nature.
one_line: An essay on autumn 2023 birdwatching at four local sites, showing how watching birds with local enthusiasts brings calm, patience and connection to nature.
key_facts: The essay is set in autumn after September 1, 2023, and visits four wildlife watching spots.
Fairview Park is a city park where the author met retired teacher and birdwatcher Bob McAllister on a crisp morning in late September.
Bob McAllister pointed out a Northern Flicker drumming in the distance and said, "Every bird has a story."
In October the author visited Lushington Streams, where nature enthusiast Emily Waters tracks kingfishers along the water's edge each morning.
Emily Waters works at a busy law firm downtown and says her early hours with the birds help her find her center.
In early November the author visited Greystone Woods, a protected area with towering oaks and maples, and met arborist and birding aficionado James Fielding.
James Fielding compared trees to "skyscrapers with their own set of road rules" while watching a pair of nuthatches.
Delta Marshland is a renowned wetland visited as the year wound down, where biologist and wildlife photographer Andrea Zhang joined the author.
Andrea Zhang described the marshlands as "a crossroad for so many species" and a place where migratory birds tell of faraway climates and landscapes.
Through birdwatching the four people found patience in waiting, community in shared rare finds, and mindfulness in observing.
Bob McAllister, a former teacher, now guides fellow birdwatchers in avian identification and behavior.
The author names resilient chickadees and migrating geese as birds that teach lessons about joy in little things and about journey and return.
